title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a traffic stop on July 23 on Calle Duran. A Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, reading the final digit as 7 instead of 2, and flagged the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers pulled over Jaclynn Gonzales, age 21, and her 12-year-old sister, identified as DD, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police cars before discovering the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another police vehicle.

The sisters, with their mother Janice Gonzales filing for the minor, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was stopped and forced to kneel after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits were filed January 3 and are pending in state District Court.
